state.description:
Closes #132

## What changed

- **Server timeout.** The first load waits 4 s for our server's response headers, then uses the bundled snapshot. Only the wait for headers is timed, so a slow 4 MB NEO body from a live server is never cut off.
- **Background retries.** While a dataset shows the snapshot (or nothing), it asks the server again after 4, 8, 16, 32 s and then every 60 s, with 30 s per attempt, and swaps to the answer without a reload. The NEO catalog does the same through its worker, so the swarm also goes live. Any answer from the server ends the retries, even the server's own snapshot when JPL is down.
- **Banner.** One line under the top bar while any dataset is on the snapshot: "Live JPL data unavailable · showing the snapshot from <date>". It disappears after the swap.
- **Selection survives the swap.** The selected approach and CME move to their rows in the new list, by key, with no camera flight. A row the new list no longer has is cleared (an approach through `clearApproach`, so the camera returns to Earth).
- **No WebGL2.** A notice page replaces the app: what Perihelion is, why it cannot run, three release stills (WebP, at most 173 KB each) and links to the data sources. `?webgl=off` forces it in dev, and in that case no WebGL context is created.

The review proposals and what was built are recorded in the plan's Task 5 section. There is no wake-up `/api/health` call: the server only answers `/health`, and the first dataset request wakes Render anyway. A note was added to Task 9.

## Verification

- `npm run check` green: 1,508 tests; initial JS 372,826 B gzip (budget 380,000 B).
- Chrome, dev, 1920×809 canvas at DPR 1 on the S2721HN (75 Hz). A listener that accepts connections and never answers stood in for an asleep server.
  - The snapshot and banner appeared at 4.6 s.
  - 2026 RP39 and 2024 SH7 played through their passes from the snapshot. The card values match the snapshot rows (Phase 5 deferred check).
  - With the real server started, all three datasets went live within 26 s. The banner went away, and 2024 SH7 stayed selected and highlighted.
  - Frame times across the swap: 1,920 frames over 26 s, none over 16.7 ms (worst 14.5 ms).
- `?webgl=off` showed the notice with no canvas and no data requests.

state.description:
Closes #134

Plan Task 7: accessibility and reduced motion, with review proposals 1–9 (plan Task 7, "As built").

## Changes

- **Reduced motion.** `CameraRig.flyTo` makes every flight a cut when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` matches. It is read on every call, so a change applies to the next flight without a listener. The opening's skip uses the same helper (`scene/camera/motionPreference.ts`). Fades stay, since they move nothing.
- **Status pill.** The `<summary>` no longer has `aria-live`, because its age changes every minute. A hidden polite live region beside the pill says only "Data status: <head word>".
- **Event lists.** The approach and CME lists are one Tab stop each (roving `tabIndex`), with ↑/↓/Home/End inside. The Tab stop is the last focused row, else the selected row, else the first.
- **Sliders.** The scrubber speaks the date instead of a Julian Date number, and the speed slider speaks its rate (`aria-valuetext`).
- **Landmark.** The scene is wrapped in `<main>`, which was the only audit Lighthouse failed on `main`.
- **Tests.** New tests cover the rig cutting under reduced motion, the motion helper, the roving-row logic, one Tab stop per list, the pill announcing only its head word, the `<main>` landmark, and accessible names for every button, input and select in seven panels. `FocusPicker` gained a server snapshot (the same reader) so it renders in that last test.

The planned test "the pill has `aria-live`" became "only the head word is announced" (proposal 3, approved).

## Verification

- `npm run check` passes: 1,464 tests; initial JS 371,194 B gzip (budget 380,000 B).
- Keyboard only (Chrome, dev, live data): pick an approach, play it, pick a CME, watch it and change the speed all worked from the keyboard. A full Tab cycle is 19 stops with 100 approach rows listed.
- Lighthouse desktop on `vite preview`: Accessibility 100 (was 98), Performance 100, TBT 0 ms, CLS 0.015.
- Reduced motion: checked by stubbing `matchMedia` in the page. A flight had landed two frames after `flyTo`, while the same flight without the stub was still at eased progress ≈ 0. The macOS setting itself was not toggled, so that acceptance box is still open.
